news_title: CFS finds excessive Bacillus cereus in preserved bean curd sample from Kung Wo Beancurd Factory - Dimsum Daily
efet_title: Food Alerts / Allergy Alerts - CFS finds excessive Bacillus cereus in sample of preserved bean curd
efet_body:
CFS finds excessive Bacillus cereus in sample of preserved bean curd
Issue Date
12.10.2026
Source of Information
Food Surveillance Programme of Centre for Food Safety (CFS)
Food Product
Bottled preserved bean curd
Product Name and Description
Product name: 公和荳品廠 — 玫瑰腐乳 (No product name in English)
Net weight: 340.5 grams
Sales period of the affected batch: September 24 to October 9, 2026
Place of origin: China
Reason For Issuing Alert
The CFS collected the above-mentioned sample from a retailer in Shum Shui Po for testing under its routine Food Surveillance Programme. The test result showed that the sample contained Bacillus cereus at a level of 140 000 per gram.
According to the Microbiological Guidelines for Food, if ready-to-eat food contains Bacillus cereus at a level of more than 100 000 per gram, it is considered unsatisfactory.
Bacillus cereus is commonly found in the environment. Unhygienic conditions in food processing and storage may give rise to its growth. Consuming food contaminated with excessive Bacillus cereus or its heat-stable toxins may cause gastrointestinal upset such as vomiting and diarrhoea.
Action Taken by the Centre for Food Safety
The CFS has informed the retailer concerned of the issue, and instructed it to stop sale, remove from shelves and recall the affected batch of the product.
A preliminary investigation by the CFS has found that the affected batch of the product comprises only 48 bottles, 26 of which were sold at the retailer between September 24 and October 9. The retailer has voluntarily surrendered the remaining products from the same batch to the CFS for disposal.
Advice to the Trade
Stop using or selling the affected batch of the product immediately if in possession.
Advice to Consumers
Not to consume the affected batch of the product.
Further Information
The CFS press release
Members of the public may call the retailer’s hotline at 4621 7383 for enquiries regarding the recall of the batch of the product concerned.
Centre for Food Safety
Food and Environmental Hygiene Department

news_title: CFS urges public not to consume two kinds of imported prepackaged salad and pesto products suspected to be contaminated with Salmonella - www.info.gov.hk
efet_title: Food Alerts / Allergy Alerts - Not to consume two kinds of imported prepackaged salad and pesto products suspected to be contaminated with Salmonella
efet_body:
Not to consume two kinds of imported prepackaged salad and pesto products suspected to be contaminated with Salmonella
Issue Date
9.10.2026
Source of Information
Food Incident Surveillance System of the Centre for Food Safety
Food Product
Prepackaged salad and pesto
Product Name and Description
Product name: Nutrient Dense Nutty Super Wholefood Salad
Brand: Marks & Spencer
Pack size: 285 grams
Place of origin: United Kingdom
Use-by date: October 8, 2026; October 9, 2026; October 10, 2026; October 11, 2026
Importer: ALF Retail Hong Kong Limited
Product name: Collections Pistachio Pesto
Brand: Marks & Spencer
Pack size: 115 grams
Place of origin: United Kingdom
Use-by date: October 8, 2026; October 9, 2026; October 10, 2026; October 11, 2026; October 12, 2026; October 13, 2026
Importer: ALF Retail Hong Kong Limited
Reason For Issuing Alert
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) through its Food Incident Surveillance System, noted notifications from the Food Standards Agency of the United Kingdom and the Food Safety Authority of Ireland that the above-mentioned products might have been contaminated by Salmonella and are being recalled.
Upon learning of the incident, the CFS immediately followed-up the cases. A preliminary investigation found that the above-mentioned importer had imported and sold the affected products.
Salmonella infection may cause fever and gastrointestinal upset such as vomiting, abdominal pain and diarrhoea. The effects on infants, young children, the elderly and persons with a weak immune system could be more severe and may even lead to death.
Action Taken by the Centre for Food Safety
The importer concerned has stopped sales, removed from shelves the affected products and has initiated a recall according to the CFS's instructions.
The CFS will alert the trade to the incident, and will continue to follow up and take appropriate action. The investigation is ongoing.
Advice to the Trade
Stop using or selling the affected batches of the products immediately if they possess them.
Advice to Consumers
Stop consuming affected batches of the products.
Further Information
The CFS press release
Members of the public may call the importer’s hotline at 8 0093 1457 during office hours for enquiries about the recall.
Centre for Food Safety
Food and Environmental Hygiene Department
2026-10-9
